::: proof

$\text{RSS}$ is a quadratic function of $(\intcoef, \coef{x})$,
so we find where its partial derivatives are zero,
then check that this point is the unique minimum.

The derivative with respect to $\intcoef$,
by the chain rule applied to each term of the sum:

$$
\frac{\partial \text{RSS}}{\partial \intcoef}
= \sum_{i=1}^n 2 (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
  \frac{\partial}{\partial \intcoef} (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i).
$$

The inner derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial}{\partial \intcoef} (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&= \frac{\partial y_i}{\partial \intcoef}
  - \frac{\partial \intcoef}{\partial \intcoef}
  - \frac{\partial (\coef{x} x_i)}{\partial \intcoef}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= 0 - 1 - 0
&& \text{($y_i$ and $\coef{x} x_i$ do not depend on $\intcoef$)}\\
&= -1
\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the inner derivative back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial \text{RSS}}{\partial \intcoef}
&= -2 \sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{n \bar{y} - n \intcoef - \coef{x} n \bar{x}}
&& \text{($\sum_i y_i = n\bar{y}$, $\sum_i x_i = n\bar{x}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Setting it to zero and dividing by $-2n$ gives
$\bar{y} - \intcoef - \coef{x} \bar{x} = 0$,
so $\intcoef = \bar{y} - \coef{x} \bar{x}$.

The derivative with respect to $\coef{x}$,
again by the chain rule applied to each term:

$$
\frac{\partial \text{RSS}}{\partial \coef{x}}
= \sum_{i=1}^n 2 (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
  \frac{\partial}{\partial \coef{x}} (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i).
$$

The inner derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial}{\partial \coef{x}} (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&= \frac{\partial y_i}{\partial \coef{x}}
  - \frac{\partial \intcoef}{\partial \coef{x}}
  - \frac{\partial (\coef{x} x_i)}{\partial \coef{x}}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= 0 - 0 - x_i
&& \text{($y_i$ and $\intcoef$ do not depend on $\coef{x}$)}\\
&= -x_i
\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the inner derivative back in,
and substituting $\intcoef = \bar{y} - \coef{x} \bar{x}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial \text{RSS}}{\partial \coef{x}}
&= -2 \sum_{i=1}^n x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-x_i$)}\\
&= -2 \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \paren{(y_i - \bar{y}) - \coef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})}
&& \text{(substitute $\intcoef$)}\\
&= -2 \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x}) \paren{(y_i - \bar{y}) - \coef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})}
&& \text{(subtract $\bar{x} \sum_i \paren{(y_i - \bar{y}) - \coef{x} (x_i - \bar{x})} = 0$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{S_{xy} - \coef{x} S_{xx}}
&& \text{(definitions of $S_{xy}$ and $S_{xx}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The subtracted sum in the third step is zero
because $\sum_i (y_i - \bar{y}) = 0$ and $\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x}) = 0$.
Setting the derivative to zero gives $\coef{x} = S_{xy} / S_{xx}$.

This stationary point is the unique minimum.
The matrix of second derivatives of $\text{RSS}$ is

$$
2 \begin{pmatrix} n & n\bar{x} \\ n\bar{x} & \sum_i x_i^2 \end{pmatrix},
$$

whose top-left entry $2n$ is positive and whose determinant is
$4\paren{n \sum_i x_i^2 - n^2 \bar{x}^2} = 4 n S_{xx} > 0$.
So the matrix is positive definite,
$\text{RSS}$ is strictly convex,
and its only stationary point is its global minimum.

:::
